newsitem.title: FRANCE: All European states have right to join NATO - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: All European states have right to join NATO - Chirac.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, speaking on the day of a U.S.-Russian summit about NATO enlargement, said on Thursday all European countries had a right to join the Atlantic alliance.

Chirac's office said he made the comment in a meeting with visiting Slovakian Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, whose country is not expected to be in the first group of former-communist countries invited to join the Western defence alliance.
"For France, all European countries have a right to enter NATO," officials quoted Chirac as saying.
The aim was to erase the Cold War division of Europe which resulted from the Yalta summit at the end of World War Two, he said.

He was speaking as U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin, meeting in Helsinki, were to discuss Western plans bitterly opposed by Moscow to admit some former communist East European states to NATO.
Chirac set no date for his aim, nor did he spell out where he considered the borders of Europe stopped.

French officials have said neither Russia nor Ukraine or Belarus are candidates for NATO membership but have left open the question of the three former Soviet Baltic republics, which are candidates to join the European Union.

Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary are widely expected to be the first new members invited to join the alliance at a NATO summit in Madrid in July. France and Italy are pressing for Romania and Slovenia to also be in the first wave.

Chirac's office said Meciar, who made no comment to journalists after the meeting, was satisfied with French assurances that all candidates for EU membership should start negotiations on an equal footing.
He was also told that France would support Bratislava's bid for membership of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), a think-tank of rich industrial nations.
